glosses: to scowl, frown
Contracter, plisser son visage en signe de mécontentement.

examples.text: En fait Simon ne pensait qu’à fuir, qu’à me fuir. Il fallait le retenir de force. Je lui dis qu’il faisait marcher les langues tous ces jours-ci. Il se renfrogna.
Au lieu de ça, je vis son reflet penché vers moi et la soudaine contrariété qui renfrognait son visage et j’ai pensé « Seigneur Jésus…! ».

Debout, auprès de lui, Hitler le couve du regard ; il en subit le charme ; il est comme fasciné, hypnotisé ; quand le Duce rit, il rit ; si le Duce se renfrogne, il se renfrogne ; c’est une véritable scène de mimétisme ; […]
Il avait cette capacité reconnue de tous à se renfrogner, comme un bélier coincé dans une bergerie.

glosses: A wrinkling of the forehead with the eyebrows brought together, typically indicating displeasure, severity, or concentration.

examples.text: Philip had once told him of a man who had a horse-shoe frown, and Tom had tried with all his frowning-might to make a horse-shoe on his forehead
He encounters some obstacle in his train of reasoning ... and then a frown passes like a shadow over his brow.

glosses: A downturn of the corners of the mouth, typically expressing sadness.

examples.text: The smile and the frown are both indicated and the operation of a motor driven flasher causes the face to look happy and sad in turn.

glosses: Any facial expression that indicates disapproval or displeasure.
To have a frown on one's face.

examples.text: She frowned when I told her the news.

glosses: To manifest displeasure or disapprobation; to look with disfavour or threateningly.

examples.text: Noisy gossip in the library is frowned upon.
The sky doth frown and lower upon our army.

glosses: To repress or repel by expressing displeasure or disapproval; to rebuke with a look.

examples.text: Let us frown the impudent fellow into silence.

glosses: To communicate by frowning.

examples.text: Frank frowned his displeasure with my proposal.
As the band paused between songs, a gust of wind blew a distinctive Worthy Farm odour in the direction of drummer/vocalist Julien Ehrich: “Wow,” he frowned, “this place smells of cow shit.”

glosses: The wrinkling of the brows or face in frowning; the expression of displeasure, sullenness, or discontent in the countenance; an angry frown.

examples.text: She made a scowl.

glosses: Gloom; dark or threatening aspect.

examples.text: Mr. Pynsent, who had asked Miss Amory to dance, came up on one occasion to claim her hand, but scowls of recognition having already passed between him and Mr. Arthur Pendennis in the dancing-room, Arthur suddenly rose up and claimed Miss Amory as his partner for the present dance […]

glosses: To wrinkle the brows, as in frowning or displeasure; to put on a frowning look; to look sour, sullen, severe, or angry.

examples.text: She scould, and frownd with froward countenaunce

glosses: To look gloomy, dark, or threatening; to lower.

examples.text: The scowling heavens.

glosses: To look at or repel with a scowl or a frown.

examples.text: to scowl a rival into submission

glosses: To express by a scowl.

examples.text: to scowl defiance
